Subject: Interested in a Reserved/Private serving walkthrough (self-signup)

Hi Ben —

We submitted a self-serve sign-up yesterday and selected the "Dedicated / Reserved" demo path. We're evaluating Redwood for an internal inference tier that needs predictable tail latency and high throughput for document vectorization at scale.

A few quick details up front so we can cut to specifics on the call:
- Expected QPS: 1,200 sustained during peak windows (20–30 minute bursts)
- P95 latency target (token generation): < 150ms for short requests (~64 tokens)
- Typical request size: 64–256 tokens; occasional long runs for batch re-embed (up to 2k tokens)
- Data residency: US-only, would be a Dedicated pool or Private VPC slot

Can we book a 45-min technical walkthrough that covers: capacity planning, autoscale behavior for burst traffic, and what fallback looks like if a pool is saturated? We attached a quick throughput profile CSV.

Thanks —
Alex Park
Head of ML Ops, Quantiflow AI

- Do those 1,200 QPS numbers represent concurrent token-generation requests or embed-only calls?
- Are the short requests mostly inference/generation (chat-like) or embeddings?
- Do you have hard SLA requirements for token-level tail latency, or is 150ms a target you want us to operate under during peak?
- Any on-prem/VPC constraints we should know about?

- Wed Aug 11, 11:00–11:45
- Wed Aug 11, 15:00–15:45

I put Markus on the thread to lead the technical portion. If those slots don't work, share a calendar link and we'll adapt. Thanks for the details, Priya — that's exactly the kind of shape we need. Two notes from the engineering side before the demo so we can make the session actionable:

1) Capacity draft: for 1,200 sustained QPS embedding-only with 64-token median, a conservative starting Dedicated pool: 8 x A100-equivalent instances (or equivalent vGPU mix) with automatic burst allowance. We will show cost vs. latency tradeoffs.

2) Burst testing plan for the demo: we'll run an isolated synthetic load for 12 minutes to reproduce the 20–30 minute burst profile (trimmed) and surface P95 across the pool. We'll demonstrate autoscale ramp-down behavior and our fallback routing (to a lighter-quant model variant) in case you need immediate continuity.

3) Pre-demo requests for you: please confirm the typical request concurrency per request (are clients sending parallel requests or single-threaded?), and if you can provide a synthetic client or a timing pattern you want us to replay, upload to the Drive link you got from Ben.

I can host the technical portion on Wed Aug 11 at 11:00 PDT and will bring a small runbook and a Jupyter-based load generator.
